problem: VLN models are limited by scene data (meshes, panoramas, video) with low fidelity, poor interactivity and no dynamic humans, and by the lack of a unified data, simulation, benchmark and model stack. Imitation-only policies are also concentrated around expert trajectories and suffer from covariate shift.
motivation: 3DGS renders photorealistic views close to the real images that VLMs were pretrained on, so rendered data can unlock VLM navigation ability. Human-robot interaction in dynamic scenes and BEV spatial memory are underexplored. Pure SFT leaves policy entropy low, so RL from SFT gives little gain.
key_idea: Build a 3DGS-based stack (GN-Matrix data, GN-Bench simulator/benchmark with dynamic avatars and BEV, GN-BAE model) and train a Qwen3-VL navigation model with SFT, then DAgger, then DAPO RL, using tokenized trajectories and optional BEV memory.
insight: The ablation shows the SFT to DAgger to DAPO order matters. On the FPV variant, w/o DAPO drops unseen SR from 38.9 to 28.1 and w/o DAgger drops seen SR from 46.9 to 26.5. The paper argues DAgger raises the low policy entropy left by SFT so that RL can explore. BEV helps on seen scenes (SR 58.6 vs 46.4) but not on unseen SR (38.5 vs 38.9), suggesting imperfect map cues can bias decisions in new scenes.
method: GN-Matrix data: 3DGS scenes from InteriorGS (1,000), handcrafted large scenes (150) and WorldGrow-expanded scenes (1760 6x6 and 240 8x8) with HSSD asset replacement. Dynamic SMPL-X-bound Gaussian human avatars (176 identities). Goal, instruction and human-following missions generated from A* paths with diversity filtering and action rebalancing.

GN-Bench simulator: diff-gaussian-rasterization rendering of RGB, depth and orthographic metric BEV. Discrete VLN-CE actions or global waypoint actions, dilated-occupancy collision handling via Bresenham, A* oracle planner, avatar rigid-transform rendering.

Trajectory tokenization: discrete action tokens (<FWD> 0.25 m, <LEFT>/<RIGHT> 15°, <STOP>) and normalized BEV waypoints as 1000 bin tokens <0>..<999>. Predicts the next 6 actions and a 3 m, 12-point BEV trajectory. FPV memory is a 4x4 mosaic of the last 16 action-step views.
SFT stage: full fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL with autoregressive cross-entropy, vision LR 2e-6 and projector/LLM LR 1e-5.
DAgger stage: 284k closed-loop samples relabeled by A* plus MPC oracle, 5 epochs at LR 1e-6, with a forced STOP heuristic. It relaxes policy over-concentration to give RL a higher-entropy start.

DAPO stage: GRPO-style group advantage with 8 samples per prompt, asymmetric clipping, no KL, vision tower frozen, 2 epochs, batch 64, 22k rollout samples as reward reference. Reward combines trajectory/heading consistency, first action, collision, length and format penalties.

Action Expert: a NavDP diffusion-policy adapter without depth input, trained from scratch with separate follow and planning experts. It converts BEV waypoints into low-level actions, loss 0.8 act + 0.2 critic + 0.5 aux.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL (fully fine-tuned with SFT, DAgger, DAPO) + NavDP-style diffusion Action Expert (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: GN-Matrix synthetic 3DGS navigation data (paper text says 47M sequences), 284k DAgger samples, 22k RL rollout samples. No real robot data.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (FPV) with 16-frame action-aligned history, optionally plus BEV and occupancy maps
setting.action_space: discrete VLN-CE actions (FWD 0.25 m, TURN 15°, STOP) and 3 m BEV pixel waypoint trajectories, executed via Action Expert
setting.privileged: none at test time for FPV; BEV/occupancy maps are given as input in the BEV variant

numbers.extra: trained with GN-Matrix data; specifics of any R2R-CE training data not stated

numbers_note: GN-Bench is a new benchmark; the 'seen'/'unseen' splits are mapped to val-seen/val-unseen. The paper reports OS, which is recorded as OSR. The Table 4 ablation full-pipeline values differ slightly from Table 1 (e.g. seen FPV SR 46.9 vs 46.4). No real-world numbers are given.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, GN-BAE reaches 3.50 NE, 75.6 OS, 67.7 SR and 63.4 SPL from single-view RGB, beating CorrectNav (65.1 SR, 62.3 SPL) and DualVLN (64.3 SR). On GN-Bench unseen, the FPV variant gets 38.9 SR versus 24.0 for the best fine-tuned baseline InternNav-S2†. The BEV variant reaches 58.6 SR on seen scenes.
limitations: The BEV variant does not beat FPV on unseen SR (38.5 vs 38.9) and shows a seen-to-unseen gap, and absolute SR on GN-Bench stays below 40 in unseen scenes.
Real-world evaluation is qualitative only, with no quantitative metrics, and inference runs on an H100 rather than the onboard edge device.
The human-following and dynamic-avatar benchmark is not quantitatively evaluated in the reported results. Several dataset statistics are left as placeholders.
